summary.prose: This Story adds Scope -- the type naming which review family and chain depth a review attempt covers -- plus two dedicated validators, validateDesignScope and validateCodeScope, that enforce exactly which named fields a Scope must carry at its own depth and reject any Pointer-typed field whose path escapes the registered repo root. The build is three Tasks: land the types, implement the validators over one shared declarative field-requirement table (closing a cross-LLD security gap by also calling Story s1's path validator), then write the full named test suite.

tasks.title: Add Scope, ValidationResult and ScopeFieldRequirement types
tasks.summary: Add interface Scope {scopeType, scopeLevel, def?, hld?, lld?, plan?, tasks?, extension?, amendment?}, type ScopeType/ScopeLevel, interface ValidationResult {ok, violations}, type ScopeValidator, and the internal (non-exported) ScopeFieldRequirement declarative table shape to src/workflow/artifact-core/types.ts, beside Story s1's Locator/Pointer. Every named Scope field is independently typed (never a generic map), per k1.
acceptanceChecks: Scope, ScopeType, ScopeLevel, ValidationResult and ScopeValidator are exported from types.ts with exactly sc3's interfaceSketch field shapes (readonly, optional-with-undefined per repo convention)
A Scope with distinct def/hld/lld/plan/tasks/extension/amendment Pointers keeps each field independently addressable (no generic map)
tsc --noEmit passes with the new types in place

tests.name: Scope, ScopeType, ScopeLevel, ValidationResult and ScopeValidator are exported with the exact documented field shapes

tasks.title: Implement validateDesignScope and validateCodeScope
tasks.summary: Add a private declarative (scopeType, scopeLevel) -> required/must-be-absent field table and one shared comparison engine in a new src/workflow/artifact-core/scope-checks.ts, then export validateDesignScope and validateCodeScope (each ScopeValidator-typed) as thin closures over that engine (alternative a1). Each validator first checks scope.scopeType matches its own dedicated literal, then the self-inclusive field-presence table, then calls sc6's validatePointerPath (from pointer-checks.ts) against every populated Pointer-typed field, folding any violation into the same ValidationResult.violations array.
acceptanceChecks: validateDesignScope/validateCodeScope return ok:false with a named violation when called on the wrong scopeType
A field required at the Scope's own declared scopeLevel being absent, or a field deeper than scopeLevel being populated, each returns ok:false with a named violation (self-inclusive chain, ac2)
An invalid (scopeType, scopeLevel) combination with no table entry returns ok:false naming the combination itself, not a field-level error
scope.tasks as an empty array at a scopeLevel requiring tasks is treated as absent
Both validators call validatePointerPath against every populated Pointer-typed field and fold ok:false violations into the same violations array (sc6 consumption, closes the cross-LLD security gap)
Neither validator performs file I/O itself

tests.name: validateDesignScope and validateCodeScope are exported with their documented signatures and enforce the field-presence table and sc6 path validation, with no file I/O

tasks.title: Write unit and integration tests for Scope and its validators
tasks.summary: Add flat kebab-case *.test.ts files under src/workflow/artifact-core/__tests__/ covering: Scope's independently-addressable named fields and a minimal valid design-review Scope, the self-inclusive depth model, each validator's exact field-presence enforcement per (scopeType, scopeLevel), and the sc6 PointerPathValidator integration rejecting an escaping Pointer path -- one test case per testStrategy.testLevels subject, matching ac1/ac2/ac3's acceptanceMapping verbatim.
acceptanceChecks: Every subject named in the LLD's testStrategy.testLevels has a corresponding test case
ac1, ac2 and ac3's provingTests from the LLD's acceptanceMapping all pass
npx tsx --test for the new test files passes with zero failures

validateDesignScope returns ok:true when scopeLevel='hld' and both def and hld are populated
validateDesignScope/validateCodeScope return ok:false with a named violation when called on the wrong scopeType

extension and amendment populated or absent independent of scopeLevel do not affect ok/violations
validateDesignScope returns ok:false with a named violation when a populated Pointer-typed field's path escapes registeredRepoRoot
validateCodeScope returns ok:false with a named violation when a populated Pointer-typed field's path escapes registeredRepoRoot
